answer: A seed bank stops fake agents with a deposit per applicant. The applicant opens a jar for a 60 dollar fee and a 150 token deposit. The jar holds 200 kernels of grain under a quartz lid sealed with umber wax. The bank sprouts 20 kernels over 14 days and logs the rate against the intake photo. A broken seal or failed test forfeits the deposit and bars the applicant 180 days. Forging 10,000 deposits freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 600,000 dollars in fees. A seed jar works like a library book one reader holds: while it is out the shelf stays empty, so a fake jar is caught at the tray.
